name: Jointed timber pile-dwellings at Hemudu, lower Yangtze
summary: Builders at Hemudu in the lower Yangtze joined the timbers of raised pile-dwellings with mature mortise-and-tenon joints about 7,000 years ago.
description: At the Neolithic site of Hemudu in Zhejiang, raised-floor (ganlan) timber buildings used technically mature wooden joints, including double-layer and dovetail tenons, about 7000 BP (about 5050 BCE after conversion). The source traces the earliest forms of ganlan pile-dwelling to this site and says its joinery is regarded as the origin of Chinese timber construction. In central Europe, Tegel and colleagues report two Linear Pottery wells, built in 5099 and 5098 BC, whose basal frames used mortise-and-tenon joints, so Hemudu is not earlier; no source opened shows contact between the two.

impact.note: The source describes pile-dwellings of this kind across southern China and Southeast Asia and calls Hemudu's joinery the origin of Chinese timber construction (reach 2); framing without lashings was a new building capability (depth 2); generativity is held at 1 because descent of later bracketed framing from Hemudu itself is asserted, not shown.

date.label: c. 7000 BP (c. 5050 BCE)
date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: Mature mortise-and-tenon joints at the Hemudu site are dated to about 7000 BP, which is about 5050 BCE when converted by subtracting from 1950.

evidence.supports: Archeologically, the Hemudu site (ca. 7000 BP) has revealed mature mortise-and-tenon joints
evidence.locator: Discussion of Ganlan types; the Introduction adds that Hemudu revealed double-layer and dovetail tenons in Ganlan buildings

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated evidence found for this capability in this community. No review has yet confirmed that nothing earlier exists.

unresolved.note: The date rests on a passing 'ca. 7000 BP' in a 2026 paper on later ganlan architecture; it should be replaced by radiocarbon dates from the Zhejiang excavation reports for the earliest Hemudu layer.
Hemudu coordinates were entered from memory (Yuyao, Zhejiang) and not taken from a fetched source.
Whether the central European and Yangtze joinery traditions were independent is not settled by the sources opened.
The lead places this in construction.shelter while the concept register lists the concept under construction.structures.

research.note: Central European wells with the same joint are as early or slightly earlier, and no source opened says whether the Yangtze joinery arose without knowledge of other woodworking traditions, so neither first_known nor independent is established.
